answers.children: Silky Terriers are moderately good with children because their small 8-10 lb size and spirited confidence make them playful yet quick to issue a warning snap when small hands tug the long silky coat. Their terrier independence means patience runs short during rough play, and the bold personality that once hunted vermin can lead to standing ground against toddlers. The breed’s alert nature adds liveliness but requires careful matching with gentle older kids. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Silky Terriers do not always get along with other pets because their vermin-hunting background gives them strong prey drive toward small animals while their confident independence creates wariness or tension with larger dogs. The long silky coat can become tangled during rough interactions, and the spirited attitude leads them to hold ground rather than yield. Same-sex aggression appears in some individuals.
answers.exercise: Silky Terriers need 30 to 45 minutes of daily exercise split into brisk walks and short play sessions because their Australian terrier ancestry supplies bursts of spirited energy that turn destructive without an outlet. They dart after leaves or toys with quick terrier speed rather than endurance running, and mental tasks prevent boredom that leads to shredded pillows or digging.
answers.shedding: No — Silky Terriers shed little despite the long silky coat because the single-layer texture traps minimal undercoat and produces low year-round hair loss. The flowing blue-and-tan strands require regular grooming to stop mats yet leave far less debris on furniture than double-coated breeds of similar size.
answers.hypoallergenic: Silky Terriers carry a long silky coat that produces little loose hair around the house. The coat still sheds minimally and requires frequent grooming to prevent mats, yet no breed is genuinely hypoallergenic and the Silky Terrier is not usually suggested to allergy sufferers.
answers.training: Silky Terriers are not the easiest to train because their stubborn independence and confident terrier spirit resist commands that lack clear purpose, while intelligence of seven makes them quick to learn when motivated. The breed was developed to hunt vermin without constant human direction so biddability is moderate and patience is essential for consistent results.
answers.lifespan: Silky Terriers live 12-15 years and their small 8-10 lb build with robust health score of six supports a typical toy-breed span when weight stays controlled. The long silky coat and spirited activity level help maintain muscle tone but the independent nature can lead to self-directed exertion that influences overall condition.
answers.size: Adult Silky Terriers reach 8-10 lb and stand 9-10 in at the shoulder so the breed feels surprisingly solid for its toy proportions with a bold stance that belies the dainty height. The flowing silky coat adds visual volume while the compact Australian terrier frame allows them to curl on laps yet still dash through tight spaces with agility.
answers.barking: Silky Terriers bark frequently because their alert and confident temperament drives them to sound off at every perceived threat or passing movement. The vermin-hunting background honed a vocal style that once warned of rats and now fills homes with insistent yaps at birds or strangers, making the barking score of seven a daily reality.
answers.apartment: Yes — Silky Terriers can live in apartments because their small 8-10 lb size and modest exercise needs fit indoor routines while the long silky coat sheds little around furnishings. Their spirited energy is met with short play rather than long runs, though the barking at perceived threats needs management to avoid disturbing neighbours.
answers.first-time: Silky Terriers are not ideal as a first dog because their stubborn independence and high barking level demand consistent leadership that novices often struggle to supply. The bold personality wrapped in a long silky coat rewards patient owners yet the vermin-hunting drive for self-directed activity can overwhelm those without prior terrier experience.
